answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities by requiring each identity to lock a refundable bond before earning, tied to a verifiable work record. Every completed job adds a signed entry to the agent's history graph, where each job is a vertex linked to the client who paid and the peers who checked it. A newcomer starts thin, like a single dune in an open field, while a trusted agent shows a dense, layered history, like shale built over time. Faking hundreds of identities then means locking a bond and forging a full history for each, so fraud costs more than honest work.
